newsitem.title: EGYPT: Sudan's Mahdi calls on armed forces to mutiny.
newsitem.headline: Sudan's Mahdi calls on armed forces to mutiny.

text.p: Sudanese opposition leader Sadeq al-Mahdi on Tuesday urged Sudan's armed forces to overthrow Khartoum's Islamist government which he said had ruined the country.

Mahdi, who fled Khartoum for Eritrea in December and is currently on a tour to bolster support for the opposition, said in a statement faxed to Reuters that there were signs that Sudanese civilians were thinking of a popular revolt.

A coalition of northern and southern opposition forces began attacking Sudanese army units along the eastern border of the country nine days ago in what they say is a bid to pressure the Khartoum government and pave the way for a popular uprising.
Sudanese President Omar Hassan al-Bashir has said Ethiopia and Eritrea are behind the fighting and issued a mobilisation call but both countries deny the charges.

"I tell our country's armed forces and police that your true front is in Khartoum and that your humanitarian, national, and faithful duty is to take sides with the people and to move firmly to topple the corrupt regime that rules Sudan today," Mahdi said.

"I assure you that in this way you will be paying penance for the wrongs committed in your name, spare the people's blood, and open the way to peace and to a system of governing that is based on the people's acceptance," he added.

Mahdi was democratically elected prime minister of Sudan in 1989 when the present government seized power in a military coup. He is the leader of the powerful Umma Party and of the Ansar, the religious movement loyal to the 19th century Mahdi.

Mahdi said Khartoum's present rulers had stoked the fires of the civil war in the south by introducing religion into the conflict, ruining Sudan's economy and also bringing relations with its neighbours to the brink of war.

"There are signs that people are moving towards an uprising and it has become obvious that the Sudanese armed forces, no matter how hard the regime tries to tame them, will perform their historic role and take the side of the people," Mahdi said.
